newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mondragon up 6.77 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Mondragon up 6.77 pct in late trade.

text.p: Gaming firm and resort developer Mondragon International Philippines Inc rose 65 centavos, or 6.77 percent, to 10.25 pesos in late trading on Friday after the company announced positive forecasts for 1996 and 1997 earnings, brokers said.
"I suspect the rise is on the net income news," said Spencer Yap, research head at BPI Capital Corp.

Mondragon in a statement issued before the close of trade on Friday said it expects a 430 million peso net profit in 1996 compared to 216 million pesos in 1995. For 1997, the firm said it estimates profits at 650 million pesos.

Yap said Mondragon shares were in negative territory for most of the session on news concerning a dispute with the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor), the state-run agency that granted the company the permit to operate casinos at the Clark Special Economic Zone in the northern Phiippines.
Pagcor claimed Mondragon violated provisions of the permit, which the company has denied.
Mondragon had asked the Philippine Stock Exchange for temporary suspension of itsshares as they could have been adversely affected by the dispute.
The Manila bourse rejected the company's request on Friday.
